key_idea: Lexicographic order here is ASCII order (digits < uppercase < lowercase), while numeric order is by length first and then by base-62 digit value at the first difference.
sketch: For each pair compute lexLess = (a < b) with ordinary string comparison, and numLess = shorter length, or for equal lengths compare the digit values (0-9, a-z=10..35, A-Z=36..61) at the first differing position. Print YES iff they agree. The first sample (icpc vs ICPC -> NO) confirms the lexicographic comparison is ASCII, not digit-value order. O(total length); use fast input for 2e6 characters. No leading zeros and distinct strings mean no further corner cases.
